headline: Ishraque Hossain calls reports of resignation order a rumor
summary: The State Minister for Liberation War Affairs denies claims that the Prime Minister asked him to step down following a controversial weapon display.
details: State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain has dismissed reports that he was ordered to resign from the cabinet as a 'rumor'.
In an audio message shared on Sunday, the minister stated that there is no truth to these claims and any such decision would be announced officially via a press conference, not through rumors.
The Ministry of Liberation War Affairs also issued a statement calling the news 'false, fabricated, and motivated', asserting that the minister continues to perform his duties with dedication.
The controversy stems from an incident on Saturday where Ishraque Hossain and his associates were seen with weapons during an anti-drug drive in Gendaria, where six people were detained.
The minister has previously explained his position, stating that the weapons were displayed for self-defense during the social resistance program against drugs.

However, the Dhaka Metropolitan Detective Branch (DB) is investigating whether the display of weapons was lawful. They have stated that action will be taken if any irregularities are found in the investigation.
caption:
Is State Minister Ishraque Hossain resigning? The minister and his office have officially dismissed the reports as 'fabricated rumors'.

State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain has dismissed reports that he was ordered to resign from the cabinet as a 'rumor'.

In an audio message shared on Sunday, the minister stated that there is no truth to these claims and any such decision would be announced officially via a press conference, not through rumors.

The Ministry of Liberation War Affairs also issued a statement calling the news 'false, fabricated, and motivated', asserting that the minister continues to perform his duties with dedication.

The controversy stems from an incident on Saturday where Ishraque Hossain and his associates were seen with weapons during an anti-drug drive in Gendaria, where six people were detained.

The minister has previously explained his position, stating that the weapons were displayed for self-defense during the social resistance program against drugs.

However, the Dhaka Metropolitan Detective Branch (DB) is investigating whether the display of weapons was lawful. They have stated that action will be taken if any irregularities are found in the investigation.

headline: ACC approves charge sheet against Saima Wazed over WHO post
summary: The daughter of ousted PM Sheikh Hasina is accused of providing false information in her CV to secure a high-ranking position at the WHO.
details: The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has approved a charge sheet against Saima Wazed, daughter of ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, regarding her appointment as regional director for the WHO’s South-East Asia region.

The ACC investigation alleges that Saima Wazed provided false information in the CV she submitted to the WHO, specifically claiming she had worked as an honorary specialist or expert at Bangladesh Medical University (formerly BSMMU).
The inquiry found that she allegedly used this false information and abuse of power to obtain the position, which the commission says tarnished the country’s reputation.
The case was filed with the ACC’s Dhaka-1 integrated district office on March 20, 2025, and was investigated by Tahasina Munabil Haque, deputy director of the ACC’s Money Laundering-1 branch.
The probe report states that at the time of application, Saima Wazed was the chairperson of the National Advisory Committee on Autism and Neurodevelopmental Disorders and the Suchona Foundation.

The commission also alleges that she exerted pressure to have her CV forwarded to the WHO headquarters in Geneva through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Bangladesh’s Permanent Mission to the UN, bypassing official verification processes.
According to the investigation, she subsequently secured the WHO position using the disputed information in her CV.
caption:
